title: Evidence before intelligence:
description: A transparent account of AMLOK’s public-data experiments, the measurements they support, and the work still required for lending decisions.
abstract: A risk graph becomes useful when its relationships can be traced, its claims tested, and its uncertainty inspected. AMLOK’s research release 0.3 supplies two starting points: supervised learning on structured US loan records and evidence retrieval from financial reports. Together they establish reproducible baselines; they do not establish an end-to-end underwriting model. [@results]
evidence: This report synthesizes published AMLOK experiments and their downloadable artifacts. Its scope is public SBA loan records and financial-report evidence, not private-lender outcomes or an end-to-end product validation. Dataset inventories retain their source-specific units, and proposed graph methods remain separate from measured baselines. [@datasets][@card]
takeaways: The held-out SBA cohort contains 11,996 observations and 210 reported charge-offs within the defined horizon. [@results]
BM25 retrieves all annotated evidence within five candidates for 61.81% of FinQA questions. Evidence retrieval remains a material bottleneck. [@results]
A reliable research programme needs point-in-time data, independent cohort checks, and prospective workflow evaluation before a production-performance claim.

sections.title: Start with the unit of evidence
paragraphs: A transaction, a financing announcement, and an annual-report fact answer different questions. Joining them can create context; counting them together can create a misleading impression of scale. The first research obligation is to preserve the original unit and the conditions under which it was observed.

AMLOK’s inventory includes 2,207,426 SBA loan-program rows and 208,818 New York mortgage originations from the 2024 HMDA slice. The Canadian disclosure collection contains 1,049 rows, while the SEC source contains 3,905,397 numeric facts. None of these totals is interchangeable with unique borrowers, funded facilities, or validated closed deals. HMDA origination records do not supply subsequent repayment outcomes. [@datasets]

The proposed graph should therefore retain typed relationships: an entity owns an account, a facility funds a borrower, a statement reports a balance. Each relationship needs evidence and dates. Entity resolution should attach a confidence and review state rather than silently merging similar names. Provenance is a useful organizing principle because it preserves how a claim was produced, not just its latest value. [@graph][@prov]

sections.title: Define a narrow, observable target
paragraphs: The supervised experiment asks whether an eligible SBA observation has an SBA-reported charge-off within 36 calendar months of first disbursement. This is deliberately narrower than every economic definition of default. A late payment, a restructuring, and a charge-off are different events; replacing one with another changes the task.

The cohort is an approximately 10% deterministic record-hash sample of eligible funded-status observations approved between 2010 and 2016, taken from the 30 September 2026 source snapshot. Invalid dates, unknown statuses, missing required amounts, and charge-off records without outcome dates are excluded. Those choices improve interpretability but also define a selected population. [@results]

Training uses 2010–2013 approvals, validation uses 2014, and evaluation uses 2015–2016. Exact normalized name/state groups appearing earlier are removed from later partitions. That reduces obvious overlap but cannot resolve every alias, owner, or related company. Evaluation should therefore describe the remaining entity uncertainty rather than call the split perfectly borrower-independent.

sections.title: Read the metrics together
paragraphs: Logistic regression reaches an evaluation AUROC of 0.72284; histogram gradient boosting reaches 0.71820. AUROC describes ranking across positive and negative observations. It is not an approval accuracy, a probability of repayment, or the proportion of losses avoided. The paired interval for boosting minus logistic regression spans −0.02406 to +0.01278, so this run does not establish a reliable winner. [@baseline-artifact]

Average precision is 0.04577 and 0.04267 respectively. The outcome prevalence is 210 ÷ 11,996, or about 1.75%. That context matters for a rare outcome: a model can improve ranking while still presenting many false positives at a chosen operating point. The Brier scores of 0.01706 and 0.01708 should also be interpreted alongside prevalence and a constant-prediction comparator, not in isolation.

Both models use structured fields including approval amount, guarantee fraction, initial interest rate, programme, industry, business-age category, and rate type. They exclude outcome fields and borrower names. However, the current snapshot does not prove that every retained predictor equals its original underwriting-time value. That unresolved availability question limits a prospective interpretation. [@results][@leakage]

sections.title: Test the evidence before testing the answer
paragraphs: The second experiment evaluates lexical retrieval on all 1,147 FinQA test questions, drawn from 380 source filenames. Candidates are sentences and table rows from the supplied report. Column headings remain attached to rows. Neither ranker sees the answer, reference programme, gold evidence identifiers, or the dataset’s pre-existing retrieved inputs. Gold annotations are used only after ranking. [@results][@finqa]

TF-IDF and BM25 use the same candidate construction and tokenizer. BM25 uses k1 = 1.5 and b = 0.75; one configuration per method was evaluated, without tuning against test labels. The paired gain in mean Recall@5 is 4.31 percentage points, with a 95% interval of 2.37–6.22 points from 2,000 source-filename bootstrap resamples. Rounded table values yield a 4.30-point subtraction; the reported paired gain uses unrounded scores. [@retrieval-artifact]

Complete evidence is the stricter operational question. BM25 finds every annotated item within five candidates for 61.81% of questions, leaving 38.19% incomplete by this definition. That complement is a calculation, not a measured answer-error rate. An answer model might fail with complete evidence or succeed using other information; neither outcome was tested here.

figure.label: Measured · 1,147 FinQA questions
figure.caption: Percentages use AMLOK’s document-local candidate sets. Recall averages the fraction of gold evidence retrieved per question; complete evidence requires all annotated items. These are distinct metrics.

sections.title: Make the graph hypothesis falsifiable
paragraphs: The next useful question is whether relationships improve decisions beyond the same underlying records. A graph experiment should compare an identical population and feature window with and without relationship features. Freeze the entity-resolution rules before the held-out test and examine false merges separately from missed connections.

Borrower, connected-group, time, and institution splits answer different generalization questions. A temporal split tests a later period. A connected-group split tests separation from known networks. An institution holdout tests transfer across operating contexts. None should be substituted for another without explaining what changed.

For each candidate improvement, predefine a target, horizon, baseline, primary metric, missing-data policy, and uncertainty method. Report results by source coverage and cohort. A lift that exists only for well-connected, long-tenured businesses may not help a new applicant with sparse records. The current published baselines do not measure that lift. [@evaluation][@card]
bullets: Reconstruct what was available at the decision date, including document publication delays.
Run ablations for identity links, transaction relationships, and document evidence.
Inspect calibration and review burden at the institution’s proposed operating points.
Reserve a prospective period to measure actual workflow outcomes after the research protocol is fixed.

sections.title: Reproduce first, extend second
paragraphs: The research package links a baseline result manifest and record-level predictions, plus a retrieval manifest, item-level rankings, source analysis, and acquisition records. Reproduction should preserve the dataset snapshot, preprocessing rules, scoring definitions, and seeds. A changed upstream file is a new version of the experiment, even if the URL remains the same. [@reproduce]

An institutional pilot should begin with a frozen research specification and a representative authorized dataset. Compare the proposed workflow against the existing process, log overrides, and distinguish time saved from credit outcomes. Review turnaround, evidence completeness, missed events, calibration, and loss experience belong in separate measurements.

The scientific contribution at this stage is a visible evidence trail and honest baselines. The published studies support research into connected risk intelligence. They do not establish a production foundation-model checkpoint, Canadian lending-score validity, or superiority to hosted frontier models. Those are separate claims that need separate experiments. [@card]
sections.takeaway: Treat every performance claim as a compact contract: population, target, horizon, inputs, comparator, metric, uncertainty, and exclusions. If one is missing, the headline is not yet decision-ready.

title: Follow the receipts.
description: A merchant cash advance guide to settlement timing, recurring cash generation, and contract-aware stress testing.
abstract: Merchant finance depends on the conversion of sales into usable cash. That conversion can be interrupted by refunds, processor reserves, seasonality, or competing obligations even when gross sales look healthy. This guide builds a reviewable cash-flow assessment around the actual settlement chain. [@mca]
evidence: Historical US research provides context; the operating examples are explicitly hypothetical CAD scenarios. No AMLOK merchant-loss model, advance-size recommendation, or universal remittance threshold is validated by this guide.
takeaways: Reconcile a sale through refunds, fees, reserves, and bank settlement before calling it available cash.
Separate a weak trading period from a broken data connection or shifted settlement schedule.
Evaluate the actual contract and existing obligations; gross receipts alone do not establish capacity.

sections.title: One sale, several observations
paragraphs: A point-of-sale order, processor transaction, settlement batch, and bank deposit can describe the same underlying sale. Adding them as independent revenue inflates the business. A useful record links these observations while preserving their different dates, amounts, and source identifiers. Transfers between the merchant’s own accounts should also remain distinct from customer receipts. [@record][@embedded]

Build the reconciliation by settlement batch where possible. Start with captured sales, subtract refunds and chargebacks, then account for processing costs, reserve movements, and other adjustments. Compare the calculated payout with the bank receipt after allowing for the processor’s timing conventions. An unexplained residual should remain visible; forcing it into revenue creates false certainty.

Keep the customer order date, capture date, settlement date, and bank posting date separately. A long weekend can shift receipts without changing economic activity. A settlement hold can leave sales intact while reducing liquidity. The analytical response should depend on which part of the chain changed.

sections.title: Use cash buffers as context
paragraphs: JPMorgan Chase Institute’s historical US study used 597,000 small businesses observed from February through October 2015. Median cash buffer days were 27; the 25th and 75th percentiles were 13 and 62. The measure divides average daily cash balances by average daily outflows. These are descriptive findings from a selected historical sample, not current Canadian MCA policy thresholds. [@chase]

For an individual merchant, first decide what cash can actually be used. Restricted reserves, tax amounts held for remittance, or balances in an inaccessible account may not support near-term operations. Then align the denominator with the question: normal operating outflows, all scheduled payments, or a stressed spending plan produce different runway measures.

A low buffer may reflect a deliberate sweep arrangement rather than distress. A high balance may reflect a recent financing deposit rather than operating resilience. Record the explanation and assess the time series. The ratio should open a review of liquidity, not end it.

sections.title: Work through a settlement bridge
paragraphs: Consider a hypothetical merchant with CAD 120,000 in captured monthly sales. Refunds are CAD 6,000, processing fees CAD 3,000, and the processor adds CAD 4,000 to reserves. Ignoring other adjustments, the expected settlement is CAD 107,000. A bank feed showing CAD 107,000 is consistent with the bridge; counting both sales and the bank receipt would incorrectly report CAD 227,000 of economic inflow.

Now assume operating cash costs of CAD 82,000 and scheduled remittances of CAD 18,000. The simplified monthly residual is CAD 7,000. If captured sales fall 15%, refunds remain 5% of sales, fees remain 2.5%, the reserve addition stays CAD 4,000, and other costs remain fixed, settlement becomes CAD 90,350. The residual becomes negative CAD 9,650.

This calculation isolates sensitivities. It does not establish what the merchant legally owes in the stressed month. Percentage-based remittance, reconciliation rights, reserve rules, and contract-specific provisions may change the cash schedule. Model those terms directly and show when a calculation assumes fixed payments. [@mca]

sections.title: Find the source of volatility
paragraphs: Compare like with like: weekday to weekday, trading week to trading week, and comparable seasonal windows. Document closures, channel changes, and incomplete observations before interpreting a movement. A rolling average can smooth genuine noise while also concealing a recent break, so show both the current window and its reference period.

Inspect customer and channel concentration as well as totals. A merchant can maintain revenue while becoming dependent on one marketplace or buyer. Refund timing, dispute volumes, and reserve changes help explain the quality of those receipts. A category label without a source transaction should be treated as an inference that a reviewer can challenge.

External research can motivate which patterns to examine; it cannot supply the merchant’s missing data. Missing settlement files should produce a coverage exception. They should not be converted into zero sales, nor should last month’s complete data be silently presented as current. [@monitor]
sections.takeaway: The most useful first question is often “What changed in the evidence?” before “What changed in the business?”

sections.title: Evaluate the review process
paragraphs: A pilot should compare a frozen set of merchant files under the current review process and the proposed evidence-led process. Measure reconciliation completeness, unresolved residuals, reviewer agreement, and time to a documented decision. Track which sources were missing; otherwise a faster result may simply reflect easier cases.

If later studying repayment outcomes, define the contract-specific event, observation horizon, and treatment of renewals before scoring. Separate merchants and related entities across partitions and preserve a later evaluation period. Report uncertainty and performance by channel, season, and evidence coverage. Operational improvements should not be described as lower losses unless loss outcomes were actually measured. [@evaluation]

In AMLOK’s product framing, underwriting assembles the baseline and monitoring follows changes. The institution remains responsible for the decision and the response. A useful handoff includes the settlement bridge, obligations, assumptions, disputed classifications, and the next review date, rather than just a single score. [@mca]

title: Exposure changes.
description: A whitepaper on connected evidence for trade credit insurance, from buyer concentration to invoice-level review.
abstract: In trade credit insurance, the insured business, its buyers, its invoices, and the policy are different objects. Their relationships determine how a financial change should be investigated. Connecting those objects can make a review more precise without treating every anomaly as a covered claim. [@insurance]
evidence: This is a methodological whitepaper, not an actuarial pricing study. All portfolio amounts below are illustrative CAD examples. The discussion concerns trade credit; it does not validate life, health, motor, premium-finance, or surety models.
takeaways: Measure concentration at the relevant economic group, while retaining separate legal entities.
A deterioration signal is not a coverage determination; policy terms and claim facts need their own review.
Test evidence quality and review consistency before asserting a loss-ratio or pricing benefit.

sections.title: Keep four records distinct
paragraphs: An invoice records an obligation between a seller and a buyer. A payment records movement against that obligation. A policy defines a contractual relationship with conditions, limits, exclusions, and dates. A claim records an asserted covered loss and its subsequent handling. Combining them into a single “risk record” can erase the distinctions that matter most.

A proposed evidence model should link these records without making them identical. Preserve the original invoice value, due date, disputes, partial payments, and currency. Attach the buyer’s legal identity, any related-group hypothesis, and the evidence supporting that relationship. Keep policy versions and applicable periods so that a later contract change does not rewrite an earlier assessment. [@insurance][@record]

For example, a late invoice may be disputed, extended by agreement, or partly paid. Those explanations have different implications. A monitoring system should route the case with the relevant evidence and unresolved questions, rather than infer a covered default from lateness alone.

sections.title: See concentration through relationships
paragraphs: Consider a hypothetical receivables book of CAD 1 million. Buyer A owes CAD 350,000, B owes CAD 250,000, C owes CAD 200,000, and D owes CAD 200,000. The largest legal-name exposure is 35%. If A and B are verified members of the same economic group, the connected group represents 60% of the book.

The amounts have not changed. The interpretation has. One shared dependency may affect more exposure than the legal-name view reveals. Conversely, an unverified name match should not automatically consolidate buyers. Review the ownership evidence, effective dates, and degree of control, and preserve the ability to reverse a mistaken connection.

Group concentration is still not expected loss. Contracts, guarantees, payment terms, jurisdictions, and risk mitigants can differ within a group. Use the connected view to prioritize a review, then inspect the underlying obligations. A single concentration percentage cannot encode every contractual distinction. [@graph]

sections.title: Separate changing exposure from changing data
paragraphs: A buyer’s apparent arrears can rise because an invoice feed arrives before a payment file. A customer may move to a different billing entity. An accounting-system migration can create duplicate open items. Before assigning economic meaning, reconcile observations across sources and record when each became available.

Use aging buckets with explicit definitions. For example, “days past due” should reference the contractual due date and reflect approved extensions consistently. Separate disputed items, credits, and pending cash application from undisputed overdue balances. If a policy or reporting convention requires a different treatment, make that difference visible rather than burying it in a transformation.

The monitoring baseline should include the last reconciled state, source completeness, and outstanding exceptions. A review can then ask whether exposure increased, payment timing worsened, coverage changed, or information became less reliable. These are different causes and should not share an undifferentiated alert. [@monitor]

sections.title: Measure the right denominator
paragraphs: Claims frequency, overdue-invoice share, and loss ratio describe different populations. A claim count needs an exposure definition and time window. An overdue-invoice measure can be weighted by count or amount. A loss ratio requires consistent premium and loss recognition conventions. Never label all three “risk rate.”

For a hypothetical invoice sample, 20 overdue invoices among 200 is a 10% count-based rate. If those invoices represent CAD 150,000 out of CAD 1 million outstanding, the amount-weighted rate is 15%. Neither is a claims frequency. Including this distinction in dashboards helps reviewers understand whether a movement reflects more cases, larger cases, or both.

When evaluating a proposed signal, preserve a future outcome window and account for policies or invoices that have not yet matured. A short observation period can miss later claims. An apparent improvement may also reflect changed underwriting or collection practices rather than a better model. The study design should describe those competing explanations. [@evaluation]

sections.title: Put governance inside the evidence flow
paragraphs: EIOPA’s August 2025 opinion addresses AI governance and risk management in European insurance supervision. It provides jurisdiction-specific context for proportional oversight, rather than a certification for a particular product. An institution should determine the requirements relevant to its own deployment. [@eiopa]

Our proposed operational design makes review possible at the level of the claim: the source invoice, the inferred relationship, the calculation, and the reason for escalation. Permissions should follow the purpose for which the data is used. A reviewer should be able to distinguish an observed fact from a model inference and record a correction without destroying the original record.

A practical pilot can measure duplicate-invoice detection, reconciliation coverage, time to resolve exceptions, and agreement on escalation. Only a separate outcome study can support statements about claim reduction or pricing accuracy. The current AMLOK research baselines do not establish insurance-loss performance. [@card]
sections.takeaway: Connected evidence is most valuable when it makes the next question specific: which buyer, which obligation, which policy, which change, and who needs to review it?

title: The mortgage after
description: A guide to affordability, renewal scenarios, and the evidence that connects an origination decision to the years that follow.
abstract: A mortgage is assessed at a moment in time and repaid over many years. Income, obligations, household spending, property value, and interest-rate terms can change on different schedules. A useful risk view preserves the original assumptions and distinguishes new evidence from a new interpretation. [@mortgage]
evidence: The Canadian macro indicators below describe groups of borrowers, not an individual’s mortgage risk. The household budget is hypothetical and is not a qualification test. No mortgage repayment model has been validated by this guide.
takeaways: Track affordability and collateral separately; neither one replaces the other.
Match the definition and timing of income, housing costs, debts, and property values.
Keep scenario results conditional on their assumptions and preserve the lender’s policy and human decision.

sections.title: Build two connected views
paragraphs: The affordability view asks whether the household can meet its obligations under a specified income and expense path. The collateral view asks what supports the exposure if repayment fails. A borrower can have substantial equity and still face immediate cash-flow pressure. Another can maintain payments while a falling property value reduces collateral protection.

Preserve income source, period, gross/net convention, stability, and verification method. Housing costs should identify which items are included, such as principal and interest, property taxes, heating, or relevant fees. Other obligations need a consistent payment basis. Ratios computed from mismatched periods or definitions can look precise while answering the wrong question. [@mortgage][@consumer]

Property value also needs a date and method. An appraisal, an automated estimate, and a current sale price are not interchangeable. Record prior liens and the exposure included in a loan-to-value calculation. Monitoring should update the evidence without overwriting the original underwriting record.

sections.title: Interpret household stress with its definition
paragraphs: The Bank of Canada’s 2026 Financial Stability Report describes roughly 2.5% of borrowers without a mortgage and 1.3% of mortgage holders as more than 60 days late on at least one account. This is a borrower-level measure across accounts. It is not a 90-day mortgage-arrears rate and does not show that taking a mortgage causes lower risk. [@boc]

The comparison illustrates why population definitions travel with every statistic. Mortgage holders can differ from other borrowers in income, assets, age, credit access, and selection. Applying an aggregate group rate to a particular applicant would discard that context. Use macro evidence to frame review priorities and scenarios, then assess the household using its authorized records.

When monitoring changes over time, keep the delinquency definition, account coverage, and population stable. If one period uses any-account arrears and another uses mortgage-only arrears, the trend is not comparable. A dashboard should expose that discontinuity rather than connect the numbers with a smooth line.

sections.title: Stress the residual, not just the ratio
paragraphs: Consider a hypothetical household with monthly take-home income of CAD 7,000. Mortgage payments are CAD 2,400, other housing costs CAD 600, essential non-housing costs CAD 2,400, and other debt payments CAD 600. The simplified residual is CAD 1,000 before unmodelled discretionary spending and saving.

Assume the mortgage payment increases by CAD 500 at renewal, with every other input unchanged. The residual falls to CAD 500. If take-home income also falls by 10%, the residual becomes negative CAD 200. This is arithmetic under specified assumptions, not a forecast of the household’s behaviour or a substitute for a lender’s qualification rules.

The example shows why a combined scenario matters: two manageable changes in isolation may interact. A useful review considers available savings, the timing and duration of the shock, realistic spending flexibility, and any relevant assistance process. It should not infer distress solely because a stylized scenario is negative.

sections.title: Make renewal a scheduled evidence review
paragraphs: A review window should be anchored to the actual contract and renewal date, not a generic calendar alert. Record the remaining amortization, current payment structure, and assumptions used in any alternative payment calculation. Distinguish a known contractual change from a market-rate scenario.

Where new financial records are authorized, compare them with the origination baseline on a consistent basis. Changes in payroll timing, account coverage, or household composition may require interpretation. A missing account should reduce confidence in the view; it should not be treated as a disappearance of the associated obligations.

The review packet should show what changed, the source of the change, the periods compared, and unresolved questions. Keep the borrower communication and institutional response separate from the analytical signal. This makes it possible to correct evidence or provide context before a consequential decision. [@monitor][@mortgage]
sections.takeaway: A renewal scenario is a conversation aid with explicit assumptions. It becomes misleading when its projected values are presented as observed facts.

sections.title: Know what the research data can test
paragraphs: AMLOK’s published inventory includes 208,818 New York mortgage origination records from the 2024 HMDA slice. Those data describe originations and contain privacy-modified fields. They do not supply subsequent repayment histories, so they cannot establish a mortgage-default prediction result on their own. [@datasets]

A repayment study would need an authorized outcome source, a documented linkage method, a precise event definition, sufficient follow-up, and a realistic point-in-time feature view. Calibration and errors should be inspected across relevant cohorts and data-coverage conditions. Any institution-specific rule must be evaluated in the population where it will be used.

Until those requirements are met, the defensible contribution is better evidence organization, transparent calculations, and a reproducible review process. Those are meaningful operational goals, but they are different from claiming lower mortgage losses. [@evaluation]

title: Two risks inside
description: An auto-finance report on the interaction between payment capacity, vehicle exposure, and the measurement of realized loss.
abstract: An auto loan combines a household payment obligation with a changing collateral position. A stronger credit profile at origination does not eliminate payment shocks, and an apparently valuable vehicle does not guarantee a full recovery. This report separates the two risks and shows how to evaluate them together. [@auto]
evidence: This report combines dated US market observations with an illustrative CAD loss calculation. It is not an AMLOK auto-credit performance study, a Canadian market forecast, or a vehicle valuation service.
takeaways: Separate affordability, loan-to-value, and realized recovery; each has its own evidence and timing.
Compare cohorts at the same age and preserve origination conditions when studying performance.
A higher-quality origination mix and worsening delinquency can coexist; aggregates require decomposition.

sections.title: Start with the financing structure
paragraphs: New and used vehicles, loans and leases, captive and non-captive financing, and different borrower segments create different exposures. Before comparing performance, record the product, financed amount, term, rate convention, payment, down payment, trade-in treatment, and any negative equity rolled into the contract.

Payment-to-income measures need a clear income definition and payment frequency. Collateral measures need a dated value and a stated basis, such as purchase price or estimated resale value. Additional financed products and fees can increase the loan balance without increasing recoverable vehicle value in the same way. [@auto]

The evidence should allow a reviewer to reconstruct the contract economics. Keep original values as well as updates. A later vehicle estimate should not overwrite the valuation used at origination; both are necessary to understand whether exposure changed because of amortization, valuation, or a new assumption.

sections.title: Read origination trends carefully
paragraphs: The New York Fed’s February 2025 analysis reports US auto originations to borrowers with credit scores above 760 of USD 250 billion in 2022, USD 252 billion in 2023, and USD 264 billion in 2024. It also describes delinquency increases across score bands. The observations come from the Consumer Credit Panel/Equifax. [@nyfed]

There is no contradiction in those two findings. Originations are a flow of new credit; delinquency describes performance of outstanding loans over time. Changing cohort composition, economic conditions, and loan terms can affect the two measures differently. A strong aggregate origination mix is not proof that every segment is improving.

For an institutional study, compare loans at equal months on book and retain the original credit and product strata. Report how refinancing, prepayment, missing observations, and transfers are handled. Otherwise an apparently better curve may reflect different exposure duration rather than improved performance.

sections.title: Trace a loss from balance to recovery
paragraphs: Assume a hypothetical defaulted loan has CAD 30,000 outstanding. Gross vehicle sale proceeds are CAD 25,000 and recovery-related costs are CAD 2,000. With no other recoveries, the simplified net recovery is CAD 23,000 and the loss is CAD 7,000, or 23.3% of the outstanding balance.

If gross proceeds instead fall by 20% to CAD 20,000 while costs stay CAD 2,000, net recovery becomes CAD 18,000. The loss becomes CAD 12,000, or 40.0%. This is a conditional severity calculation after default. It does not estimate how likely default is.

A fuller economic analysis would identify interest treatment, fees, timing, discounting, and subsequent recoveries. A valuation at one date and a sale months later should not be treated as the same observation. Review both model error and actual changes in the asset or market.

sections.title: Connect affordability to the calendar
paragraphs: A monthly payment may be affordable on an annual income average while still conflicting with actual pay dates and other obligations. Identify the frequency and reliability of income, the schedule of payments, and the amount of accessible cash between them. A temporary timing mismatch and a persistent income shortfall require different responses.

Changes should be interpreted against the original evidence and the current coverage of connected accounts. Do not infer an income loss because a payroll deposit moved to an unobserved account. Preserve the distinction between source failure, classification uncertainty, and verified economic change. [@consumer][@monitor]

The institution’s review should determine whether a signal calls for evidence refresh, a borrower conversation, or another action under its policies. An analytical system should document the trigger and context while keeping accountability for the response explicit.
sections.takeaway: Payment capacity explains whether the obligation can be met. Recovery analysis explains what happens after it is not. A useful auto-credit view needs both.

sections.title: Design an outcome study that can be audited
paragraphs: Define events separately: a first missed payment, 30-day delinquency, repossession, charge-off, and net realized loss are not synonyms. Fix the observation horizon and determine how immature loans are treated before measuring performance. A model evaluated on short-lived accounts should not be compared casually with one evaluated over a longer horizon.

Use time-based evaluation, inspect connected-borrower overlap, and report cohort performance by product, vehicle category, and source coverage. For any proposed monitoring signal, measure warning lead time against an event defined in advance and include the false-alert workload. Aggregate ranking performance does not tell an operations team how many cases it will need to review. [@evaluation]

AMLOK’s currently published supervised results concern SBA-reported charge-offs in a US government-guaranteed business-loan sample. They do not validate auto lending. An auto-specific study needs its own authorized data, target, comparison, and uncertainty analysis. [@card]

title: One sale. Many records.
description: A whitepaper on evidence architecture for embedded finance: reconciliation, data coverage, and the boundaries of an API response.
abstract: Embedded finance brings financial decisions closer to the systems where business happens. It also creates several observations of the same event. The challenge is to preserve their relationships, resolve differences, and show what remains unknown rather than equating more integrations with more independent evidence. [@embedded]
evidence: The architecture and worked settlement example are proposed methods. The FinQA measurement is a published document-retrieval result; it is not an evaluation of an embedded-finance integration or an API’s credit decisions.
takeaways: Count economic events, not the number of systems reporting them.
Represent permission, freshness, and coverage alongside every derived financial view.
Keep observed facts, calculated measures, and model interpretations distinguishable in the response.

sections.title: Integration is the beginning of the evidence chain
paragraphs: A successful connection establishes access to a source. It does not establish that every relevant account is present, that historical coverage is complete, or that records reconcile with another system. A merchant may connect one processor but use several. A bank connection may omit a facility held elsewhere. An accounting export may contain accrual entries with no cash movement.

Treat coverage as part of the analytical result. Record the authorized source, accounts included, earliest and latest observations, refresh time, and known gaps. Derived measures should identify the exact window and inputs they used. If coverage changes, a comparison may need to be restated rather than interpreted as business growth or contraction. [@embedded][@record]

A useful API contract should make these distinctions consumable: source observations, normalized facts, linked economic events, calculated measures, and review flags. These are recommendations for response design, not undocumented promises that every AMLOK endpoint already exposes the same fields.

sections.title: Reconcile before aggregating
paragraphs: Imagine a platform records CAD 10,000 in captured sales. The processor reports CAD 500 in refunds, CAD 300 in fees, and a CAD 200 reserve addition. The net payout is CAD 9,000. A bank account then records that same CAD 9,000 deposit. The economic sale remains CAD 10,000 gross; settlement is CAD 9,000. Adding all three positive observations would incorrectly suggest CAD 28,000 in separate inflows.

A matching rule should use identifiers where available, then compatible amounts, dates, and counterparties. Timing windows need to reflect actual settlement conventions. Uncertain matches should remain candidates, not silently accepted links. One payout can cover many transactions, so the evidence graph must support aggregation relationships as well as one-to-one matches.

For analysis, keep the accounting question explicit. Revenue recognition, gross merchandise volume, processor settlement, and unrestricted bank cash are different measures. Reconciliation explains their differences; it should not erase those differences to produce a single convenient number. [@financial]

sections.title: Measure whether the evidence was found
paragraphs: AMLOK’s FinQA experiment makes a useful architectural point. BM25 retrieves all annotated support within five candidates for 61.81% of 1,147 held-out questions. The remaining 38.19% is the calculated share with incomplete evidence at that cutoff. This does not measure answer correctness, nor does it measure connected-account completeness. [@results][@retrieval-artifact]

The general design implication is to evaluate the evidence stage independently. A downstream model cannot reliably justify a calculation using a table row it never received. A plausible-looking answer can hide that failure. Coverage checks, missing-input states, and source inspection therefore deserve their own tests rather than being bundled into a single end-to-end score.

For an integration, analogous tests should use its own ground truth: expected accounts, reconciled events, known statement periods, and source availability. An improvement on a financial-report benchmark does not transfer automatically to payment reconciliation. The bridge between tasks must be tested.

sections.title: Design for interrupted connections
paragraphs: An expired authorization, a source outage, and an account with no new activity can look similar if every failure becomes an empty list. Preserve distinct states. A consumer of the API needs to know whether there are no records, whether records could not be fetched, or whether the source is no longer in scope.

Use an explicit freshness policy for each decision. Historical statements may remain useful for one analysis while being too stale for another. Retain the last successful observation without presenting it as newly observed. When a source recovers, reconcile backfilled events and avoid interpreting a batch arrival as a sudden burst of economic activity.

Corrections also need history. If a processor amends a transaction or an entity match is reversed, derived measures may change. Keep both the prior result and the revised version with the reason for revision. This makes an institutional review reproducible and gives the product team a concrete failure mode to improve. [@record][@monitor]
sections.takeaway: “Connected” should describe access. “Complete,” “current,” and “reconciled” are separate claims, each requiring evidence.

sections.title: Evaluate the platform boundary
paragraphs: A pilot should include realistic missingness and integration failures, not just fully connected demonstration accounts. Measure reconciliation accuracy against reviewed records, source-coverage completeness, duplicate handling, correction behaviour, and the ability to trace a result back to its inputs.

For predictive research, hold out entire platforms or institutions when transfer is the claim being tested. A model may learn platform-specific bookkeeping conventions that do not generalize. Separate coverage effects from model effects: a richer source set and a better algorithm are different interventions. [@evaluation]

For operational governance, assign ownership of authorization, data correction, analytical interpretation, and the final financial decision. NIST’s voluntary AI risk-management framework offers a general governance reference, but the specific controls and their effectiveness must be demonstrated in the deployed workflow. [@nist]

title: Underwrite the
description: A business-lending guide to cash conversion, financing capacity, and the relationships behind the balance sheet.
abstract: A business balance sheet describes positions; underwriting needs to understand the movements and obligations behind them. This guide connects operating cash, working capital, facilities, and related entities while retaining the source and accounting meaning of each figure. [@business]
evidence: A public issuer disclosure provides a real reconciliation example. Working-capital calculations are illustrative. Neither establishes an AMLOK borrower score or lending recommendation; entity scope and contractual terms require institutional review.
takeaways: Separate operating receipts, financing flows, transfers, and restricted cash.
A facility limit, a drawn balance, and net available capacity are different quantities.
Inspect connected obligations without assuming every affiliated entity provides enforceable support.

sections.title: Read movements as well as balances
paragraphs: Revenue, profit, operating cash flow, and unrestricted cash can diverge for ordinary reasons. Credit sales create receivables before cash arrives. Inventory absorbs funds before a sale. A loan increases cash while creating an obligation. A transfer between owned accounts moves liquidity without creating new income.

A reviewable assessment starts with a bridge between reported financial statements and the available transaction evidence. Record the period, currency, accounting basis, and scope of each source. An annual consolidated statement and a current operating-account feed may describe different entities and windows. Reconciliation should identify those differences before interpreting a mismatch as risk. [@financial][@record]

AMLOK’s public-record analysis highlights a practical example: Kinross’s March 2022 USD 1 billion term loan refinanced acquisition-related revolving borrowings. A cash inflow from that financing is not operating revenue. The issuer announcement provides the purpose and facility context that a deposit amount alone would miss. [@findings][@kinross]

sections.title: Reconcile facility capacity
paragraphs: BCE’s 2025 financial report presents CAD 6,393 million of total committed credit facilities, CAD 1,409 million drawn, CAD 71 million of letters of credit, and CAD 2,550 million of commercial paper. Subtracting the latter three from the total produces CAD 2,363 million of net available capacity. This is a dated facility reconciliation, not a cash-balance statement. [@bce][@findings]

The analytical lesson is to preserve the relationship between a facility and the obligations that consume it. A revolving commitment, an outstanding borrowing, and commercial-paper support should not be treated as unrelated sources of liquidity. Conditions, sublimits, currencies, and expiry dates can further affect access.

For a private business, request the corresponding agreements and current statements where authorized. Do not assume unused headline capacity is immediately drawable. A covenant, a borrowing-base test, or a guarantee condition may change availability. The evidence packet should identify what is observed and what still requires confirmation.

sections.title: Put a clock on working capital
paragraphs: Working-capital ratios summarize timing. A simplified cash conversion cycle is days sales outstanding plus days inventory outstanding minus days payable outstanding. Use compatible periods and definitions: receivables relative to credit sales, inventory relative to cost of goods sold, and payables relative to a suitable purchase or cost measure. A single end-of-period balance can be unrepresentative in a seasonal business.

Consider an illustrative company with 45 days sales outstanding, 60 days inventory outstanding, and 30 days payable outstanding. Its simplified cycle is 75 days. If collection slows to 60 days while the other assumptions remain fixed, the cycle becomes 90 days. At assumed annual credit sales of CAD 3.65 million, 15 extra collection days represent approximately CAD 150,000 tied up in receivables: 3,650,000 ÷ 365 × 15.

That calculation is a sensitivity, not a forecast of the company’s borrowing need. Taxes, margins, seasonality, bad debts, and payment schedules can change the result. It is nevertheless useful because the assumptions are visible and a reviewer can replace them with better evidence.

sections.title: Map support and dependence separately
paragraphs: A business can depend on an affiliate without having an enforceable right to its cash. Common ownership does not automatically imply a guarantee, cross-default, or cash-pooling arrangement. Preserve each relationship type and the source establishing it. An inferred affiliation should not silently become contractual support. [@graph]

Likewise, concentration can arise through customers, suppliers, payment processors, landlords, or related borrowers. A graph can help a reviewer see where several exposures share one dependency. It should also show when a connection is uncertain, stale, or outside the available evidence.

Prioritize relationships that change a specific question. For example: does one customer explain the receivables growth; does one affiliate account for recurring transfers; does one facility support several operating entities? A dense diagram without these questions can add visual complexity without adding decision value.

sections.title: Carry assumptions into monitoring
paragraphs: At approval, record which facts support the assessment and which assumptions matter to resilience. A projected collection improvement, a temporary reserve release, or a refinancing plan should have an owner, a deadline, and evidence required to confirm it. These assumptions are natural candidates for follow-up.

Compare later observations with the same definition and scope. A new account can increase observed cash without changing the business; a revised entity mapping can change group concentration without a new economic event. Keep those methodological revisions separate from operating changes. [@monitor]

Validation should begin with whether the system preserves and reconciles evidence correctly. A later predictive study needs a specific outcome, cohort, horizon, and point-in-time data. The public SBA baseline is useful research context, but its current-snapshot limitation and US programme population prevent treating it as a validated Canadian business score. [@results]
sections.takeaway: The best underwriting narrative explains how cash is generated, where it is committed, which relationships matter, and what would cause the institution to revisit its view.

title: Affordability
description: A consumer-credit whitepaper on income timing, financial buffers, and evidence-led review as household circumstances change.
abstract: A household can meet a monthly average and still face a cash shortfall on a particular day. Understanding affordability requires a view of recurring income, essential costs, existing obligations, accessible reserves, and the timing that connects them. [@consumer]
evidence: The external survey is a dated US population observation. Household examples are hypothetical CAD calculations. This paper proposes a review method; it does not establish a consumer-credit model, approval rule, or financial advice for an individual.
takeaways: Income level, income variability, and payment timing are separate dimensions.
Keep verified cash, inferred categories, and unobserved obligations distinct.
Use uncertainty to trigger an evidence review rather than to manufacture a precise affordability score.

sections.title: Measure the household on a consistent basis
paragraphs: Gross salary, take-home pay, benefits, transfers, and borrowing proceeds should not be aggregated indiscriminately as income. Identify each source and explain how recurring income is recognized. A transfer from savings can support a payment but does not increase recurring earning capacity. A new loan creates cash and a new obligation.

Expenses need similar care. Recurring essentials, discretionary spending, annual bills, and existing debt payments have different timing. A low-spending month may omit a forthcoming insurance renewal or seasonal utility cost. State which costs are observed, which are estimated, and which remain outside the connected accounts. [@consumer][@financial]

Affordability is also purpose-specific. A monthly residual describes one set of cash assumptions; a lender’s policy ratio may use another. Show the calculation and its intended interpretation. A clear calculation is more useful than a universal score whose denominator changes from one applicant to another.

sections.title: Financial resilience is more than current income
paragraphs: In the Federal Reserve’s 2024 US household survey, 63% of adults said they would cover a hypothetical USD 400 emergency entirely with cash or its equivalent. The definition includes a credit card paid off at the next statement. This is a self-reported response to a hypothetical expense, not an observed default rate or a finding about Canadian households. [@shed]

The result motivates a separate question about accessible buffers. Two households with similar income can have different capacity to absorb an unexpected cost. Conversely, a high balance can be earmarked for a near-term obligation. The analytical view should preserve the difference between an account balance, available liquidity, and long-term wealth.

When using a buffer measure, specify which accounts are included and whether the funds are accessible. Avoid inferring a lack of savings from incomplete connections. A household should be able to provide context or correct the underlying evidence before it influences a consequential decision.

sections.title: Compare level and timing
paragraphs: Consider two hypothetical households, each receiving CAD 4,800 per month and paying CAD 4,200 in recurring costs. Both have a monthly residual of CAD 600. Household A receives two equal payroll deposits spread across the month. Household B receives one irregular deposit near month end. If most bills fall early, their short-term liquidity paths can differ despite identical monthly totals.

A cash-calendar model begins with opening accessible cash, adds each expected inflow on its date, and subtracts each scheduled payment. The minimum balance over the window identifies a timing pressure that a monthly total can hide. Expectations should be labelled as such; a projected payroll date is not an observed deposit.

Now consider a simplified monthly stress for either household: income falls by 15% from CAD 4,800 to CAD 4,080 while recurring costs stay CAD 4,200. The residual changes from positive CAD 600 to negative CAD 120. If the household has CAD 1,200 of accessible reserves, dividing by that shortfall gives ten months in a deliberately simplified constant-gap calculation. It ignores other shocks and should never be presented as a survival forecast.

sections.title: Design a reviewable change signal
paragraphs: Changes in observed income can result from unemployment, reduced hours, a changed pay schedule, account switching, or missing data. Classification should preserve these alternatives until the evidence resolves them. A useful signal reports the observation and the uncertainty rather than collapsing both into a distress label.

Compare equivalent windows and display the records contributing to the change. If one payroll period has not yet completed, say so. If a source has stopped refreshing, show the last successful observation and the affected calculations. A system that treats missing data as zero can generate the most alarming signal exactly when its evidence is weakest. [@monitor]

An appropriate review workflow can request clarification, refresh a source, or route a case to a trained team under the institution’s policies. The signal should not itself imply a collection action or an automatic reduction in access. Institutional accountability and a way to correct evidence are part of the design.

sections.title: Validate the population and the consequences
paragraphs: A consumer-credit study needs an explicit outcome and horizon, representative authorized data, and a point-in-time feature view. It should inspect performance under different income patterns, evidence coverage, and product structures. A result from business lending is not a consumer validation.

Assess calibration as well as ranking, and inspect the workload created at the proposed review threshold. Examine errors and access implications across relevant groups using lawful, appropriate evaluation data. If the intended use changes, the evaluation should change with it. A tool designed to summarize evidence should not quietly become an unvalidated approval policy.

AMLOK’s published model card distinguishes completed structured-loan and retrieval baselines from the research programme’s broader ambitions. No consumer outcome claim follows from those baselines alone. The useful near-term standard is a process where every calculation, uncertainty, and response can be reviewed. [@card][@evaluation]
sections.takeaway: Affordability becomes more informative when it shows a household’s cash path and evidence gaps, not merely a monthly average with an unexplained risk label.

title: A connection is not
description: What a risk graph should preserve before a relationship becomes evidence in a financial decision.
abstract: A shared address or a recurring transfer can be a useful lead. It can also be a coincidence, a service relationship, or a data-quality problem. A useful risk graph keeps the observation, the inferred relationship, and the reviewer’s conclusion separate. [@graph]
evidence: This article describes an evidence-design method. The company examples are hypothetical; no graph-model performance is claimed.
takeaways: Type every relationship and retain its supporting source.
Use uncertainty to guide review, not to hide a weak match.
Test whether relationships improve a defined task before claiming predictive value.

sections.title: An edge needs a meaning
paragraphs: Imagine two businesses share a registered address. That observation does not establish common ownership. They might use the same professional-services office. A transfer between them also does not establish control: it could be a supplier payment, a loan, or a refund. The graph should store what is directly observed before adding an inferred explanation.

Give relationships explicit types and effective dates. “Shares an address,” “owns,” “guarantees,” and “paid” answer different questions. A source document may establish one of these while merely suggesting another. Preserving those distinctions keeps the diagram from overstating its evidence. [@record][@graph]

sections.title: Confidence belongs to the relationship
paragraphs: It is tempting to attach one confidence score to an entity and treat every connection as equally reliable. That loses information. A company identifier from a registry may be strong evidence of identity while an ownership inference from transaction descriptions remains weak. Each relationship should carry its own evidence and review state.

W3C’s provenance model offers a useful conceptual reference: data can retain the entities, activities, and agents involved in its production. Applied to a financial graph, that means a reviewer can inspect not only a linked fact but how the link was created. This is a design principle, not a claim that provenance alone proves the fact true. [@prov]

sections.title: A false merge can change the analysis
paragraphs: Consider a hypothetical business with CAD 100,000 in obligations and an unrelated business with CAD 300,000. A false identity merge can make the first appear to carry CAD 400,000. The arithmetic is correct; the identity assumption is not. The error can then spread into concentration measures, affordability calculations, and monitoring signals.

The correction path matters as much as the initial match. Preserve the original records, the matching rule, and the derived calculations affected by a reversal. Reviewers should be able to split an entity and recompute the view without deleting the history of why the earlier result appeared. [@record]

sections.title: Measure the benefit of the connection
paragraphs: A predictive graph claim needs a comparison against the same records without the relationship features. Separate connected groups across evaluation partitions where relevant, and inspect false merges and missed links independently. Otherwise a model may appear strong because related records leaked across the split. [@evaluation]

AMLOK’s published research includes structured-loan and document-retrieval baselines; those experiments do not establish graph-model lift. The next credible result is a controlled comparison with clear entity rules and a defined outcome. Until then, a graph’s defensible value is making relationships and questions reviewable. [@card]
sections.takeaway: A graph earns trust when a reviewer can ask “Why are these connected?” and get the source, the relationship type, the dates, and the remaining uncertainty.

title: Before the signal,
description: Why monitoring needs a versioned account of what was known, when it was known, and how it was interpreted.
abstract: A change is meaningful only relative to a comparison. Monitoring that does not preserve the original evidence and assumptions can confuse a new source, a corrected record, or a changed formula with a change in financial condition. [@monitor]
evidence: The examples are illustrative process designs. This article does not report measured warning lead time or borrower outcomes.
takeaways: Retain event time and the time the information became available.
Freeze the calculation definition as well as the original value.
Treat source changes and economic changes as different events.

sections.title: The baseline is more than a number
paragraphs: A stored monthly-revenue figure is not enough to reproduce an assessment. A baseline also needs the period, source accounts, transaction classifications, exclusions, currency, and formula version. If one of these changes, the difference may be methodological rather than economic.

Consider an illustrative merchant showing CAD 100,000 in monthly receipts at approval and CAD 130,000 later. If a second processor was connected in the later period, the observed increase may reflect better coverage. Comparing the two totals without a coverage note would suggest growth that has not been established. [@record]

sections.title: Keep two clocks
paragraphs: Event time describes when something happened. Knowledge time describes when the reviewer or system could know it. A financial statement can concern a year that ended months before publication. A backfilled transaction may arrive well after its posting date. Both dates are needed for a faithful reconstruction.

A retrospective test that uses later-published evidence as if it were known at origination can overstate usefulness. The same problem can arise in a monitoring dashboard when backfilled records appear as fresh activity. Preserve the arrival and revision history, and evaluate the system using the information actually available at each decision point. [@record][@evaluation]

sections.title: A correction is not deterioration
paragraphs: Suppose a transaction previously classified as sales is corrected to a financing inflow. The calculated operating-receipts figure falls, but the underlying business has not suddenly lost revenue at the moment of correction. The system has learned that its earlier interpretation was wrong.

A useful change log distinguishes newly observed activity, late-arriving records, source corrections, revised classifications, and formula changes. The reviewer can then decide whether to revisit the original assessment, investigate current conditions, or simply update the historical record. [@monitor]

sections.title: Evaluate the signal against its purpose
paragraphs: For a monitoring pilot, define the event that a warning is intended to precede and the action a team can reasonably take. Measure lead time, missed events, false-alert workload, and the proportion of signals with complete evidence. A count of generated alerts is not a measure of effectiveness.

Preserve a future evaluation window and avoid selecting thresholds after inspecting the outcome period. Report results under different coverage conditions. AMLOK’s current public baselines do not measure monitoring lead time, so a claim about earlier intervention requires a separate study. [@evaluation][@card]
sections.takeaway: Store the baseline as a versioned explanation. A future reviewer should be able to reconstruct both the original assessment and the reason it changed.

title: The answer is only as strong
description: What AMLOK’s financial-document retrieval experiment teaches about reviewable AI.
abstract: A fluent answer can conceal a missing table row. AMLOK’s FinQA experiment isolates the evidence-retrieval stage and shows why finding support and generating an answer need separate evaluations. [@results]
evidence: Measurements are reproduced from AMLOK research release 0.3. They concern lexical retrieval on FinQA, not an end-to-end language model, a lending decision, or a comparison with frontier models.
takeaways: BM25’s Recall@5 is 73.90%; its complete-evidence rate is 61.81%. These measure different things. [@results]
A missing evidence item is a retrieval failure; it is not automatically a wrong final answer.
A review interface should expose the source, calculation, and unresolved evidence gaps.

sections.title: Ask a narrower question first
paragraphs: The study uses all 1,147 FinQA test questions across 380 source filenames. Candidate evidence consists of the supplied report’s sentences and table rows, with column headings retained. Rankers receive the question and evidence, while reference answers and gold evidence identifiers are withheld until scoring. [@results][@finqa]

This design asks whether the necessary support appears near the top of the retrieved set. It does not ask whether a language model can compute the answer, interpret the accounting treatment, or make a credit decision. Keeping the task narrow makes the result easier to reproduce and harder to overclaim.

sections.title: Two metrics expose two failure modes
paragraphs: Recall@5 averages the fraction of annotated evidence retrieved for each question. Complete evidence@5 asks whether every annotated item is present. A method can perform reasonably on average recall while still leaving many questions with at least one missing input.

BM25 reaches 73.90% mean Recall@5 and 61.81% complete evidence@5. The paired Recall@5 gain over TF-IDF is 4.31 percentage points, with a 95% source-cluster bootstrap interval of 2.37–6.22 points. The uncertainty describes these fixed methods on this dataset, not every financial document a production system might encounter. [@retrieval-artifact]

figure.label: Measured · BM25 on FinQA
figure.caption: The measures use the same 1,147 questions but different scoring rules. Complete evidence requires every annotated supporting item within five candidates.

sections.title: Make the missing input visible
paragraphs: Imagine a calculation needs operating income and interest expense. If retrieval finds the former but not the latter, a reviewable system should identify the missing input rather than quietly substitute an unrelated figure. The source period and unit matter too: a correct number from the wrong year can produce a convincing but invalid ratio.

The interface should show the evidence used, the formula applied, and any unresolved assumption. A reviewer should be able to open the original context, challenge a classification, and preserve a correction. This turns review from an impression of whether the prose sounds plausible into an inspection of a claim. [@financial]

sections.title: Evaluate each stage and the whole workflow
paragraphs: A practical test plan separates extraction, retrieval, calculation, explanation, and the institutional response. Each stage needs an error definition. End-to-end evaluation still matters, but a single aggregate score cannot explain which component failed or how to fix it.

AMLOK’s model card explicitly distinguishes completed baselines from proposed specialist-model and frontier-model evaluations. A stronger future result should preserve that separation: publish the task, source construction, comparator, uncertainty, and failure examples. Reviewability is a property of the evidence trail, not a synonym for confident language. [@card]
sections.takeaway: Before asking whether an answer is persuasive, ask whether the system had the evidence required to support it.

title: A deposit is not
description: How financing, transfers, and settlement adjustments can change the story a bank balance seems to tell.
abstract: Cash moving into an account is an observation. Calling it revenue is an interpretation. A useful financial view preserves the source and purpose of the movement before it becomes an input to affordability or business analysis. [@financial]
evidence: The issuer example is a public disclosure. The account-reconciliation example is hypothetical and does not describe an AMLOK customer.
takeaways: Classify operating, financing, and transfer flows separately.
Use source documents to explain large or unusual movements.
Preserve uncertain classifications so a reviewer can correct them.

sections.title: The amount does not explain the purpose
paragraphs: A business account can receive customer payments, a loan draw, an owner contribution, a tax refund, or a transfer from another owned account. These movements all increase the observed balance, but they have different implications for recurring cash generation and future obligations.

AMLOK’s public-record research uses Kinross’s March 2022 USD 1 billion term-loan announcement as an example. The financing refinanced acquisition-related revolving borrowings. Treating the inflow as operating revenue would lose the obligation and the refinancing purpose. The source announcement provides context a bank line alone cannot establish. [@findings][@kinross]

sections.title: Follow the economic event
paragraphs: Consider a hypothetical business receiving CAD 50,000 from customers and CAD 20,000 from a loan. It then transfers CAD 15,000 from one owned account to another. Summing the positive entries across both accounts would produce CAD 85,000. The customer receipts are still CAD 50,000; the loan is financing, and the transfer is internal movement.

For a consolidated cash view, match both sides of the transfer and retain them in the audit trail while excluding the duplicated inflow from operating receipts. Do not delete the transactions: the movement may matter for liquidity and account-level reconciliation even though it creates no new group income. [@record]

figure.caption: CAD 50,000 customer receipts + CAD 20,000 financing + CAD 15,000 internal transfer = CAD 85,000 positive entries. The operating-receipt measure excludes financing and the duplicated transfer.

sections.title: Leave uncertainty in the record
paragraphs: Transaction descriptions are often incomplete. A name match or recurring amount may suggest a category without proving it. Record the evidence used for the classification, the confidence or review state, and any alternative explanation. A reviewer should be able to inspect a suspiciously large “sales” item before it drives a decision.

An unresolved amount can be shown in a separate reconciliation category. That is preferable to forcing every transaction into a definitive label. The residual itself can guide a targeted request for an invoice, facility statement, or explanation. [@financial]

sections.title: Compare consistent windows
paragraphs: Even correctly classified receipts can mislead when the windows differ. A five-week month, a settlement delay, or a newly connected account can change totals without a comparable change in the business. Show the observation period and coverage beside the calculated measure.

For a monitoring study, evaluate both classification quality and the resulting signal. A corrected financing classification can lower a historical operating-receipts estimate without indicating a new deterioration. Preserve the revision history so the institution understands whether the business changed or the evidence improved. [@monitor]
sections.takeaway: The defensible financial story starts with the movement, establishes its purpose, and only then turns it into a measure.

title: The credit memo should
description: Carry the assumptions behind approval into a monitoring process that can revisit them.
abstract: An underwriting decision rests on facts, assumptions, and exceptions. If monitoring retains only the final score, it loses the reasons the institution considered the exposure acceptable and the conditions that would justify another review. [@monitor]
evidence: This article proposes a review design with illustrative examples. It does not claim measured reduction in defaults or a validated monitoring lead time.
takeaways: Preserve the evidence and assumptions behind the decision.
Turn material assumptions into reviewable follow-up questions.
Record the response and outcome, not just the alert.

sections.title: What made the decision reasonable?
paragraphs: A credit memo may rely on stable customer receipts, the completion of a refinancing, or the expected collection of a large receivable. Some of these are observed facts; others are conditional expectations. They should not become indistinguishable once the decision is recorded.

For each material assumption, retain its source, the date it was made, the person or team responsible for review, and the evidence that would confirm or challenge it. An exception should have the same treatment. This creates a specific monitoring purpose rather than a generic instruction to watch everything. [@record][@business]

sections.title: Translate assumptions into questions
paragraphs: Consider a hypothetical business approved partly on the expectation that a CAD 150,000 receivable will be collected within 30 days. A useful follow-up asks whether that invoice was paid, extended, disputed, or replaced by another arrangement. A broad revenue-change alert may miss the original dependency.

The monitoring design should link the invoice, its expected collection date, and subsequent payment evidence. If the source is incomplete, the result should be “not yet verified,” not “unpaid” by default. A reviewer can then request the missing evidence or interpret the delay.

sections.title: Keep the original and the revised view
paragraphs: When an assumption changes, retain both versions. A subsequent explanation may make the new situation acceptable, but it should not rewrite what the institution knew at approval. This history supports learning about which assumptions were reliable and which repeatedly required exceptions.

The same principle applies to formulas and entity mappings. If a new account or related business is added, document the change in scope. Otherwise a reviewer may interpret a revised measure as a change in borrower behaviour. [@record]

sections.title: Measure the quality of the handoff
paragraphs: An operational pilot can assess the share of decisions with traceable assumptions, the proportion of follow-ups completed on time, the evidence completeness of review packets, and whether reviewers agree on the next action. These are useful process measures that do not require pretending a short pilot can already establish long-run credit performance.

A separate outcome study should define the event, horizon, comparator, and uncertainty. It should distinguish a signal that arrived earlier from a response that actually improved an outcome. AMLOK’s current public research baselines do not establish that causal effect. [@evaluation][@card]
sections.takeaway: A monitoring system should remember why the institution said yes and make it possible to revisit that reasoning when the evidence changes.

title: When sales rise but
description: A settlement bridge can explain the gap between a merchant’s activity and the money available to operate.
abstract: Gross sales and bank receipts move on different clocks. Refunds, disputes, fees, reserves, and payout timing can widen the gap. A merchant-finance review should explain that bridge before drawing a conclusion about capacity. [@mca]
evidence: All amounts in this article are illustrative CAD values. The scenario is an analytical example, not a merchant case study or contract recommendation.
takeaways: Reconcile processor activity to actual payouts.
Inspect changes in adjustments and timing alongside sales.
Apply the merchant’s actual contractual terms when evaluating remittances.

sections.title: A larger top line can hide a smaller payout
paragraphs: Imagine a merchant’s captured sales rise from CAD 100,000 to CAD 110,000. In the first period, refunds are CAD 5,000, fees CAD 3,000, and reserve additions CAD 2,000, leaving CAD 90,000 to settle. In the second, refunds rise to CAD 9,000, fees to CAD 3,300, and reserve additions to CAD 10,000. Settlement falls to CAD 87,700.

Gross activity grew 10%, while the expected payout fell about 2.6%. Neither number is wrong. They describe different stages of the same economic flow. A review that sees only the sales growth can miss the tightening liquidity; one that sees only the payout decline can miss its cause.

figure.title: The settlement bridge changes the story
figure.label: Illustrative · CAD thousands
figure.caption: First period: 100 − 5 − 3 − 2 = 90. Second period: 110 − 9 − 3.3 − 10 = 87.7. The bars are a worked example, not observed merchant data.

sections.title: Different causes need different questions
paragraphs: A reserve increase may be temporary, contractually scheduled, or associated with a changed processor risk assessment. Refunds may reflect seasonality, a product issue, or timing from an earlier sales period. The amount alone does not identify the cause.

Retain adjustment codes, relevant processor notices, and the sales periods to which refunds relate. If payouts are delayed, compare expected and actual settlement dates. A missing file should be classified as a coverage problem until the evidence shows otherwise. [@mca][@record]

sections.title: Keep the merchant’s contract in view
paragraphs: A simplified fixed-payment stress can be useful for sensitivity analysis, but it may not represent a contract whose remittances vary with receipts or include reconciliation provisions. The actual terms determine how a changing payout affects scheduled cash obligations.

List existing obligations and their cash timing. Do not infer that a positive monthly residual guarantees every daily payment can be met. A settlement calendar, opening accessible cash, and major operating expenses can reveal a timing pressure that a monthly average conceals. [@financial]

sections.title: Turn the bridge into a review artifact
paragraphs: A useful packet contains the two reconciled periods, the components explaining the change, outstanding mismatches, and the institutional question that needs an answer. It should make it easy to distinguish lower sales from a higher holdback or a delayed payout.

For evaluation, compare the bridge with reviewed source records and track unexplained residuals. Any claim that this analysis predicts losses needs a separate outcome study with a defined target, horizon, and cohort. Accurate reconciliation is valuable evidence; it is not itself a validated credit score. [@evaluation]
sections.takeaway: When sales and cash diverge, the gap is the subject of the review. Explain its components before interpreting its risk.
